title: Leveraging Technology for Scaling Teacher Professional Development: Insights Into Usage, Challenges, and Opportunities in Rural Tanzania
text_snippet: Leveraging Technology for Scaling Teacher Professional Development: Insights Into Usage, Challenges, and Opportunities in Rural Tanzania Purpose The article examines how technology can be leveraged to scale technology-supported teacher professional development (TPD). It explores usage, challenges, and opportunities for scaling technology-supported TPD in resource-constrained contexts. Design/Approach/Method This article employs design-based implementation research and participatory methodology, involving four iterative cycles/rounds of co-design with the Tanzania Institute of Education, to investigate the design and implementation of the government-led, technology-supported Mafunzo Endelevu ya Walimu Kazini program or Teachers’ Continuous Professional Development. Data were collected using teacher surveys, participatory focus group discussions, interviews, and observations of Community of Learning (CoL) sessions and classroom practices in 20 schools in Tanzania. Findings Teachers are using technologies, including digital platforms such as WhatsApp groups for collaborative discussions, resource sharing, and peer support, and digital CoL modules. title: Micro-Credentialing for Teacher Professional Development at Scale: A Meta-Synthesis of Technological Competence and Institutional Integration
text_snippet: Micro-Credentialing for Teacher Professional Development at Scale: A Meta-Synthesis of Technological Competence and Institutional Integration Purpose This study examines the role of micro-credentialing in teacher professional development, with particular attention to technological competence in digitally mediated educational contexts. It addresses the fragmented understanding of micro-credentialing within teacher professional development at scale (TPD@Scale) through a qualitative meta-synthesis. Design/Approach/Method A qualitative meta-synthesis was conducted in accordance with established synthesis principles. Twenty-six empirical studies published between 2020 and 2025 were identified through a systematic search of eleven academic databases and analyzed using thematic coding and interpretive synthesis. Findings The findings indicate that micro-credentials are generally perceived as flexible, practice-oriented learning opportunities that support teachers’ technological competence. They complement rather than replace traditional professional development, although their effectiveness depends on institutional recognition, digital readiness, and policy support. title: Investigating the Links Between Students’ Science Capital and Science Career Aspirations in Schools in Abu Dhabi
text_snippet: Investigating the Links Between Students’ Science Capital and Science Career Aspirations in Schools in Abu Dhabi Purpose The United Arab Emirates (UAE) requires optimal participation of citizens in its STEM workforce to develop the country's knowledge economy. In this study, students’ indications of science capital (measured by proxy using items adapted from previous survey questionnaires) were investigated to see how this construct interacted with their science career aspirations. Design/Approach/Method This study utilizes a theoretical framework of science capital wherein a combination of factors, including students’ school and home experiences of science, may indicate future science aspirations. The participants were 429 middle and high school students from government schools in Abu Dhabi. Findings Overall, it was observed that science capital performed as a significant construct in this context, and that the relationship between science capital and science-related career aspirations is positive and significant. This may be an important factor in predicting Abu Dhabi students’ future career plans. title: Developing a Model for Technology-Supported School-Based Teacher Professional Development in Ghana: Opportunities and Challenges
text_snippet: Developing a Model for Technology-Supported School-Based Teacher Professional Development in Ghana: Opportunities and Challenges Purpose The purpose of this study is to explore the opportunities and challenges afforded by a technology-based model for school-based teacher professional development (TPD) in Ghana and its implications for scaling. The Ghanaian Government requires teachers to meet regularly in professional learning communities (PLCs) to discuss and ultimately improve their practice. Design/Approach/Method The Open University and the University of Cape Coast (UCC) developed a digitally based, sustainable model for TPD. Ten schools tested this model, which could operate at scale. UCC selected a free online course that addressed policy aspirations for inclusive education. Teachers studied on their phones (2 hr a week; 4 weeks) and discussed the content of the course during weekly PLCs. A mixed-methods study was carried out using a questionnaire, interviews, and observations of PLCs. Findings The findings highlighted the relevance of the course material and the challenges involved in facilitating PLCs. Relatively little discussion took place, but the data demonstrated the potential for this model if facilitators are appropriately trained. title: Socio-Culturally Responsive VR Training for Enhancing English Teachers’ Pragmatic Competence
text_snippet: Socio-Culturally Responsive VR Training for Enhancing English Teachers’ Pragmatic Competence Purpose This study investigates the effectiveness of socio-culturally responsive virtual reality (VR) training in enhancing the pragmatic competence of English teachers, addressing the challenge of limited authentic native-speaker interaction in English as a foreign language (EFL) contexts. Design/Approach/Method A sequential explanatory mixed-methods design was employed with 122 randomly selected EFL teachers. Quantitative data were collected through pre- and posttraining verbal discourse completion tasks (DCTs), while qualitative insights were gathered through focus group interviews. The VR intervention consisted of 108 hr of fully immersive simulations featuring artificial intelligence (AI)-driven avatars portraying diverse sociocultural scenarios, speech acts, power relations, and social distances based on a human-on-the-loop (HOTL) approach. Findings Participants demonstrated statistically significant improvements in pragmatic competence, including pragmalinguistic accuracy and sociopragmatic appropriateness. These improvements were driven by immersive engagement, real-time adaptive feedback, enhanced communicative confidence, increased metapragmatic awareness, and reflective

title: Research on Policy Instruments in Education, 2005–2023: A Scoping Review
text_snippet: Research on Policy Instruments in Education, 2005–2023: A Scoping Review Purpose This review aims to describe and analyze the contributions and challenges of a body of literature on public education policies that views policy instruments as sociological institutions. Design/Approach/Method Based on a scoping review of 42 peer-reviewed articles published from 2009 to 2023 in academic journals, the paper outlines the evolution of research on the sociology of policy instruments in education, considering the main policy themes and policy instruments studied, as well as the theoretical and methodological solutions in use. Findings The review highlights the main contributions and challenges of this body of research, considering three key dimensions: the institutional elements, trajectories, and effects of policy instruments. It shows that this research has been particularly productive in analyzing the consolidation of performance-based governance; the Europeanization of education; and the legitimization of new policy actors, such as intergovernmental organizations, and private actors (at the transnational level), as well as intermediary actors (at the national and local levels). title: Reciprocal Learning Among Chinese and Canadian Educational Cultures Amid Turbulent Global Relations
text_snippet: Reciprocal Learning Among Chinese and Canadian Educational Cultures Amid Turbulent Global Relations Purpose The article's purpose is to describe the success of the Canada–China Partnership Program during a time of turbulent global relations. The project aimed to generate reciprocal learning in educational settings between Canada and China with the ultimate goal of strengthening global harmony. The project began in 2013 when global relations were positive, and by the end of the project in 2024, global relations were tense. Project participants found themselves in two environments: a positive collaborative cross-cultural school-based working relationship and a guarded environment of negative sentiment. Design/Approach/Method Project design consisted of collaborative school-based and teacher education working relations. Sister schools and a teacher education exchange structure defined a reciprocal learning working environment. Research proceeded under the methodological rubric of narrative inquiry. Findings The project's success amidst global tensions is the key finding reported herein. Content findings are in the 16-volume “Intercultural Reciprocal Learning in Chinese and Western Education” book series and in associated articles. title: Obsolete Schooling and the Courageous Minority: Rethinking Educational Change in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
text_snippet: Obsolete Schooling and the Courageous Minority: Rethinking Educational Change in the Age of Artificial Intelligence Purpose This article argues that schools must change if they are to remain relevant in the age of artificial intelligence (AI), and that the most important agents of such transformational change are the courageous minorities willing to act before the system is ready. Design/Approach/Method The article develops a conceptual analysis by bringing together recent evidence on the risks of AI and screen-based technologies with scholarship on the grammar of schooling, educational reform, and panarchy theory. Findings The article argues that current concerns about AI—cheating, weakened effort, cognitive dependence, and policy backlash—are symptoms of a deeper problem: Schools still teach and assess what AI can already do. Incremental improvement is therefore insufficient. What is required is transformational change that redefines what is worth learning and how learning should be organized. Yet such change is extraordinarily difficult because schools function as a political and social “peace treaty” that stabilizes competing interests and protects existing assumptions. title: Classroom Assessment-Informed Reflection Approach for Teacher Professional Learning: A Case From Singapore
text_snippet: Classroom Assessment-Informed Reflection Approach for Teacher Professional Learning: A Case From Singapore Purpose This study examines the development and application of the Classroom Assessment Informed Reflection Ladder (CAIRL) method to facilitate teacher reflection on classroom assessment practices, thereby fostering their professional learning. Design/Approach/Method To illustrate the use of CAIRL, we conducted a case study involving four rounds of lesson observations and post-lesson semi-structured interviews with an English language teacher at a primary school in Singapore. The data were analyzed based on three components of the laddering method—purpose, intention, and process—to identify the patterns and changes in the teacher's reflection. Findings Our study shows that the teacher initially adhered to a rigid teaching procedure, prioritizing the coverage of prescribed content and exam preparation. Through the CAIRL method, discussions were fostered between the teacher and the researcher about student learning in relation to the teacher's beliefs. This led the teacher to adapt his teaching, using students’ learning evidence as feedback to inform his subsequent teaching practices. title: How Do Chinese Graduate Students Contribute to Japanese Universities: An Agential Perspective
text_snippet: How Do Chinese Graduate Students Contribute to Japanese Universities: An Agential Perspective Purpose This study explores the intricate roles played by international students within Japanese universities through the lens of Chinese students studying in Japan. It aims to move beyond traditional views of students as passive recipients of knowledge, exploring their multifaceted contributions through the lens of knowledge diplomacy. Design/Approach/Method Employing a collaborative autoethnography (CAE) approach, the authors explored their experiences as former or current Chinese students in Japan, shedding light on the nuanced dynamics of international student mobility. By embracing an agentic perspective and the framework of knowledge diplomacy, the data analysis delineates their multifaceted role beyond agents of knowledge diplomacy across four principal dimensions: academic–formal, academic–informal, nonacademic–formal, and nonacademic–informal. Findings This study reveals their contributions not only as agents of knowledge diplomacy engaged in disciplinary learning, but also as active participants in extracurricular activities and social interactions that are integral to campus and community life. title: Conceptualizing Emergent Ocean Literacy: Exploring Sensuous and Spatial Early Childhood Education and Ecological Care Practices in Coastal Landscapes
text_snippet: Conceptualizing Emergent Ocean Literacy: Exploring Sensuous and Spatial Early Childhood Education and Ecological Care Practices in Coastal Landscapes Purpose With this article, we aim to open up and further develop the conceptualization of educational practices associated with ocean literacy (OL) by enquiring into age-appropriate practices and conceptualization. Furthermore, we aim to make ocean knowledge relevant to early childhood education. Design/Approach/Method Drawing on practices developing research inspired by utopian action research, this study enquires into children's, teachers’, artists’, and researchers’ co-exploration of local ocean landscapes and their connection to oceans through stories and world maps. The article investigates ocean literacies by researching how younger children sense, co-explore, and express their experiences in local landscapes connected to the ocean. Findings Based on the existing ocean literacy concept and literature, this study, with its detailed narrative descriptions, gives ground to propose the concept of emergent ocean literacy (EOL) to better define the youngest children's first conceptualizing of oceans and ocean landscapes and the pedagogical practices to develop a “glocal” mindset. title: The Lagoon as a Space for Thought: Transformative Narratives of Teachers
text_snippet: The Lagoon as a Space for Thought: Transformative Narratives of Teachers Purpose This article aims to explore how teachers perceive their relationship with the environment and how this perception shapes their professional identity within the Kindergarten of the Lagoon project. Design/Approach/Method Emotional textual analysis (ETA) and hermeneutic phenomenological analysis (HPA) were used to examine transformations in affective symbolization processes related to both the project and the lagoon environment. Data were collected through three focus groups with teachers, designed as reflective spaces for discussing their educational practices and professional roles. Findings The findings highlight the transformative potential of combining outdoor education and learning with structured reflective practices. Teachers reported significant changes in their connection to the environment (place-based education) and in their sense of professional identity. These shifts underscore how promoting early childhood education for sustainability (ECEfS) can reshape teaching approaches and strengthen teachers’ sense of purpose. title: Teacher Feedback and Student Social and Emotional Skills: An Empirical Study Based on Second Round of SSES 2023 Data
text_snippet: Teacher Feedback and Student Social and Emotional Skills: An Empirical Study Based on Second Round of SSES 2023 Data Purpose This study investigated student perceptions of teacher feedback in the classroom, the relationship between teacher feedback and student social and emotional skills, and the mediating role of the teacher–student relationship in the association between feedback and student social and emotional skills. Design/Approach/Methods The study used a sample of 65,612 students, comprising younger (10-year-olds) and older (15-year-olds) cohorts, from 15 cities surveyed in the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development's 2023 Survey on Social and Emotional Skills. Hierarchical linear model analysis and a mediating effect test were performed to examine the relationships. Findings Gender, age, immigrant status, and reading grades were associated with student perceptions of teacher feedback. However, the effects of immigrant status, socioeconomic status, and math grades on student perceptions of feedback differed between 10- and 15-year-olds. title: Understanding and Growing Together: Mathematics Teachers’ Reciprocal Learning Between China and Canada
text_snippet: Understanding and Growing Together: Mathematics Teachers’ Reciprocal Learning Between China and Canada Purpose This study aims to build a sustainable reciprocal learning community between China and Canada in mathematics education, exploring how teacher learning changes, and identifying factors influencing their professional growth. Design/Approach/Methods This study uses qualitative study methods, including interviews, observations, and document analysis. Four participants are involved in this 7-year project. Findings Teacher noticing emerges across three reciprocal learning phases. Mathematics teachers experience three transformation stages in cross-cultural reciprocal learning: from knowing to criticizing, from understanding to learning, and from collaborating to cocreating. Within these three stages, the study identifies specific advantages in mathematics education, highlighting its distinct cultural features within the context of cross-cultural reciprocal learning. The understanding of context (which is deemed the deep structure of culture) is important to have success in reciprocal learning between different countries. title: Toward a Progressive Model for Teaching Multigrade Classes in Zimbabwe's Fast-Track Resettlement Satellite Schools: Aligning Theory With Practice in Education
text_snippet: Toward a Progressive Model for Teaching Multigrade Classes in Zimbabwe's Fast-Track Resettlement Satellite Schools: Aligning Theory With Practice in Education Purpose Teacher development programs in most developing countries, including Zimbabwe, have remained largely theory-laden and distant from the classroom, with insufficient links to practice. This study investigates the pedagogical and management challenges faced by teachers in multigrade classes within satellite primary schools in Zimbabwe's fast-track resettlements, particularly following the Fast-Track Land Reform Programme (FTLRP) initiated in 2000. Design/Approach/Method Employing a qualitative case study design, data were collected through in-depth interviews, focus group discussions, observations, and document reviews to gain a comprehensive understanding of the challenges encountered by educators in this unique context. Findings The study found that the heterogeneous nature of multigrade classes presents significant pedagogical and management difficulties. Many teachers were unprepared to handle such diverse classrooms, leading to a pronounced disconnection between theoretical training and practical implementation. title: Reflecting on Reflective Practice: Philosophical Critique of Its Ontological Ethics and the Case for Teacher Flourishing
text_snippet: Reflecting on Reflective Practice: Philosophical Critique of Its Ontological Ethics and the Case for Teacher Flourishing Purpose This study critiques the disenchantment of contemporary reflective practice from an antique three-dimensional ethics to a shibboleth in professional education comprising an epistemology of decision-making, a techne for production, and even a neoliberal governance technology. Design/Approach/Methods Following a Foucauldian analysis of the change of truth and subjectivity in the Greco-Roman , Christianity, and post- Cartesian epochs, this study presents how reflection, once a “care of the self” technology to forge “spiritual corporality,” was overshadowed by the philosophy of “knowing yourself,” eventually being disenchanted into a secularized tool. Findings With the aim of re-enchanting reflective practice as Aristotelian virtue-phronesis in teacher education, we appeal to teachers to become students’ in loco parentis as a form of flourishing. Originality/Value This study philosophically interrogates reflective practice, which is often uncritically regarded as a self-evidently golden practice in teacher professional development.

title: Leading in the AI Age: A Systematic Review of Global Perspectives on AI and Educational Leadership
text_snippet: Leading in the AI Age: A Systematic Review of Global Perspectives on AI and Educational Leadership Purpose Amid heated global discourses on the benefits, challenges, and propositions of adopting AI in educational leadership, this study elucidates the global impacts of AI on educational leadership and how educational leaders should approach it. Design/Approach/Method Using the Responsible AI framework, this study systematically reviews literature on AI and educational leadership from 2015 to 2024. Findings AI empowers educational leadership but also brings potential costs and risks. It has been approached and applied differently in educational leadership globally, without a consensus on how to leverage it. A human-centered, symbiotic relationship between AI and educational leaders could be a future trend if leaders reconstrue, change, and adapt educational leadership through the responsible use of AI. Originality/Value This study contributes to presenting and analyzing global opinions of AI and educational leadership amid systematic differences and regional diversities in technology adoption. It advances international scholarship on the disciplinary application of AI in educational leadership and the evolving discourses surrounding educational leadership.

title: Bridging Educational Gaps in Low-Resource Classrooms: AI-Enhanced Project-Based Learning for STEM Educators in Africa
text_snippet: Bridging Educational Gaps in Low-Resource Classrooms: AI-Enhanced Project-Based Learning for STEM Educators in Africa Purpose This research examines the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Project-Based Learning (PBL) to enable science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) educators in resource-limited African classrooms to shift from content-centric teaching to competency-based learning (CBL). It seeks to ascertain how cost-effective AI tools can address deficiencies in teacher capacity, inclusivity, and digital accessibility. Design/Approach/Method Using a qualitative research design, data were collected from ten STEM educators across Nigeria, Botswana, Ghana, Namibia, and Sierra Leone through open-ended interviews, document analysis, observations, and analysis of participants’ project artefacts. The intervention involved hands-on engagement with speech-to-text-to-image generation, smartphone-based block coding using the Magnetcode application, circuit simulation, and microcontroller-based prototyping. Findings Thematic analysis revealed five outcomes: AI speech-to-text tools enhanced visualization of science concepts; smartphone-based coding increased inclusion; simulations provided cost-effective scaffolding for hardware use; educators gained transition skills in computational

title: How to Improve the Quality of Teacher–Child Interaction? A Teacher-Level Randomized Controlled Trial in Shanghai
text_snippet: How to Improve the Quality of Teacher–Child Interaction? A Teacher-Level Randomized Controlled Trial in Shanghai Purpose This research aimed to determine the impact of the Kindergarten-Based Instructional Research Model (KIRM) to promote the quality of teacher–child interaction (KIRM-TCI), a professional development training intervention focused on improving the quality of teacher–student interaction. Design/Approach/Methods The study used a teacher-level randomized controlled trial. Fifty-one pre-K teachers across four kindergartens were randomly assigned to either the KIRM-TCI condition—integrating CLASS (Classroom Assessment Scoring System) competencies with structured peer dialogue and practitioner inquiry—or a control group. Blinded observers conducted CLASS assessments before and after the intervention. Findings Within the scope of the research, it was indicated that the project had a positive effect on the quality of emotional and instructional support in teacher–child interactions (TCIs). The findings substantiate KIRM-TCI's efficacy in improving interactions, attributable to its synergistic integration of evidence-based practice with reflective professional development. title: From Assistance to Advancement: A Systematic Review of How GenAI Supports L2 Writing Learning From the Lens of Activity Theory
text_snippet: From Assistance to Advancement: A Systematic Review of How GenAI Supports L2 Writing Learning From the Lens of Activity Theory Purpose Despite the rapid proliferation of empirical studies on generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in second language (L2) writing, a systematic review of how GenAI supports L2 writing learning remains scarce. This study aims to fill this gap by providing a comprehensive synthesis of existing research. Design/Approach/Method We conducted a systematic review of 55 pertinent articles published in SSCI journals between January 2023 and July 2025, employing Activity Theory as our analytical framework. The review systematically examined six key components within the activity system: subjects (participant characteristics), tools (research instruments), community (research contexts), division of labor (social roles and power distribution), rules (procedural norms), and objects (learning goals). Findings Our analysis revealed that tools, division of labor, and rules serve as mediating components that exert both positive and negative effects on learning objects (i.e., the goals of learning activities). The framework effectively captured the complex interactions among different elements within GenAI-assisted L2 writing research. Originality/Value This study contributes to the literat

title: Preschool Teacher Professional Development for Promoting Social–Emotional Learning in Pakistan: A Quasi-Experimental Study
text_snippet: Preschool Teacher Professional Development for Promoting Social–Emotional Learning in Pakistan: A Quasi-Experimental Study Purpose This study evaluates the impact of social and emotional learning (SEL) training for Pre-K teachers on classroom dynamics and children's well-being. Design/Approach/Method Conducted in public schools across Karachi, Pakistan, the study utilized an experimental design with a sample comprising 12 schools, 24 teachers, and 410 preschoolers. Evaluation instruments included the Classroom Assessment and Scoring System (CLASS) and the Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire. The SEL teacher training program employed a locally tailored curriculum, spanning 4 months, during which teachers received both training and mentorship for implementing SEL practices. Findings Analysis revealed significant enhancements in intervention schools across all three CLASS dimensions: emotional support ( p -value .036), classroom organization ( p -value .009), and instructional support ( p -value p -value p -value p -value p -value .081), conduct problems ( p -value .087), and hyperactivity ( p -value .354). title: Emphasising Loopholes to Facilitate Early Childhood Education for Sustainability
text_snippet: Emphasising Loopholes to Facilitate Early Childhood Education for Sustainability Purpose Due to ecological changes in the world's oceans, there is an overwhelming need to foster respect for marine ecosystems and raise awareness of their protection. The authors therefore ask: How can emergent ocean literacy be facilitated in early childhood education for sustainability (ECEfS)? The aim was to identify drivers for emergent ocean literacy through collaborative exploration. Design/Approach/Method Ethnographically inspired fieldwork was conducted in two early childhood education institutions on the west coast of Norway. The practices in these institutions revealed collaborative exploration between children and teachers on the seashore. The theoretical framework for the study and the analysis is anchored in Ødegaard's idea of collaborative exploration and based on Bakhtin's concepts of dialogism, polyphony, speech genres, and loopholes. Findings The analysis surfaced place, time, and relations as relevant drivers for emergent ocean literacy through collaborative exploration. These drivers opened up for the emergence of loopholes, play as children's preferred speech genre, and dialogical relationships between children and teachers. Originality/Value The maritime envir

title: Practice and Reflection as a Dialectical Unity: Pre-Service Teachers’ Experience in a Service-Learning Program
text_snippet: Practice and Reflection as a Dialectical Unity: Pre-Service Teachers’ Experience in a Service-Learning Program Purpose This paper aims to explore how initial teacher education constructs dialectical relationships between practice and reflection through a service-learning program in response to the “double reduction” policy in China. Design/Approach/Method Drawing from a Marxist activity-theoretical view of dialectics, this study investigates a Chinese university's arrangement for developing pre-service teachers (PSTs) by means of service learning. Both quantitative and qualitative data were collected to analyze the participants’ experience in the service-learning program. Findings The service-learning program embodies a dialectical unity of practice and reflection for PSTs, which is realized through three core processes: the transformation of professional knowledge via object-oriented activity; the deliberation of teaching skills supported by knowledgeable others; and the achievement of personalized learning outcomes through the appropriation of mediating artifacts. The program thus engages PSTs in socially necessary service while structuring reflective experiences that directly enhance their professional competence. title: Mathematics Teachers’ Changes in Interdisciplinary Teaching: A Formative Interventionist Case Study in China
text_snippet: Mathematics Teachers’ Changes in Interdisciplinary Teaching: A Formative Interventionist Case Study in China Purpose This study examines changes in Chinese mathematics teachers’ beliefs and practices regarding interdisciplinary teaching and how these changes unfold. Design/Approach/Method Guided by formative interventions, this study employed the Interconnected Model of Professional Growth (IMPG) to analyze changes in the beliefs and practices of six Chinese mathematics teachers. Data were collected through videotaped discussion meetings, classroom observations, and individual interviews. Findings The Cultural-Historical Activity Theory (CHAT) model, functioning as a model/vision tool, prompted mathematics teachers to reflect on their interdisciplinary teaching practices. After offering students more inquiry-based learning opportunities, the teachers observed that students were able to address interdisciplinary problems through collaborative group work. This led teachers to recognize the value of interdisciplinary teaching, to acknowledge that students’ capacities exceeded their initial expectations, and to view themselves more as facilitators of student learning. title: How to Conduct Umbrella Review in Education? A Step-by-Step Methodological Guide Through a Case Study in Digital Diaries
text_snippet: How to Conduct Umbrella Review in Education? A Step-by-Step Methodological Guide Through a Case Study in Digital Diaries Purpose The need for scientific evidence in the field of education has accelerated the production of systematic reviews (SRs), but this effect is much less evident for umbrella reviews. This creates the opportunity to implement systematic processes capable of addressing the challenges raised by umbrella reviews in the field of education. The objective is to produce a methodological guide for carrying out umbrella reviews based on a case study, which is the use of digital diaries in education. Design/Approach/Method We carried out an umbrella review of SRs of digital diaries in education, setting out, for each phase, a brief theoretical foundation, the difficulties and possible solutions, and the case study being used as the example. Findings In relation to planning and conducting an umbrella review of SRs, we set out the methodological challenges involved in the formulation of the research question, the overlapping of primary studies, and the evaluation of methodological quality. Originality/Value In education, there are very few methodological guides on umbrella reviews. title: Intelligence Surplus: Economics of Education After Human Capital
text_snippet: Intelligence Surplus: Economics of Education After Human Capital Purpose This paper reexamines the foundations of the economics of education in the age of artificial intelligence, asking whether human capital remains an adequate analytical concept when intelligence is no longer scarce. Design/Approach/Method The study revisits the educational theories associated with five Nobel laureates (Schultz, Becker, Spence, Romer, and Lucas), and identifies five foundational assumptions: linear returns, stable depreciation, individual attribution, stable signaling, and unidirectional externalities. It develops a new conceptual framework by integrating insights from the economics of education with Bourdieu's theory of cultural capital and Arendt's conception of action. Findings The paper argues that AI disrupts these assumptions by transforming intelligence into an abundant and replicable resource. It therefore proposes Intelligence Surplus as a new analytical unit, comprising embodied, objectified, and institutionalized forms. The paper identifies the new scarcity of the AI era as meaning-translation capacity, the ability to transform unique human experience into representations that AI systems can process. title: Governing the Objectives of Higher Education: A Revisit of Confucius’ Dual Imaginaries of the Ideal Man ( Junzi ) and Social Order ( Tianxia )
text_snippet: Governing the Objectives of Higher Education: A Revisit of Confucius’ Dual Imaginaries of the Ideal Man ( Junzi ) and Social Order ( Tianxia ) Purpose This study examines the limitations of the dominant Anglo-American Research University model in addressing contemporary global challenges. By revisiting Confucius’ legacy, it explores his dual imaginaries of the ideal individual ( Junzi ) and social order ( Tianxia ) to propose a new framework for higher education. Design/Approach/Methods The study utilizes The Analects as its primary source to analyze Confucius’ educational philosophy. The “Confucius pragmatic paradigm” was adopted to interpret The Analects , which highlights the situational and participatory nature of Confucius’ dialogs, treating utterances as speech acts where the speaker's intentions are as crucial as the literal meaning. Findings This study underscores the relational, contextual, and internally driven nature of Confucius’ thought, emphasizing the organic integration of individual self-cultivation with the construction of a well-ordered society. It argues that Confucian ideals offer valuable insights for transforming higher education to better address global fragmentation and the evolving landscape influenced by AI-driven transformations. title: Outcomes and Factors of International Service-Learning From Student Perspective: A Qualitative Study in Hong Kong
text_snippet: Outcomes and Factors of International Service-Learning From Student Perspective: A Qualitative Study in Hong Kong Purpose Academic programs that combine experiential learning with international education and community engagement are widely practiced in higher education. International (or global) service learning is an example. The study explores student outcomes and factors of international service-learning programs, drawing from students’ perspectives. Design/Approach/Methods This qualitative study is based on in-depth interviews with undergraduate students ( N = 18) who participated in international service-learning programs involving multiple disciplines and project locations in a public university in Hong Kong SAR, China. Findings Four types of student outcomes are discussed: interpersonal, personal, civic, and academic. Interaction with host communities, intersubjective reflection, and meaningful service were identified as key factors in international service-learning's impact on students. Teamwork with peers and teachers’ influence are matters less discussed in literature, which emerged in the study as important factors for students. title: A Distributed Architecture Integrating Educational Philosophy and AI-Driven Learning Design: The PDP–ICEE Learning System
text_snippet: A Distributed Architecture Integrating Educational Philosophy and AI-Driven Learning Design: The PDP–ICEE Learning System Purpose Education in the age of AI faces an epistemic paradox: It can increasingly observe learning through data and analytics, yet it still struggles to understand learning as a process of meaning. While modern systems exhibit a degree of technical reflexivity, their feedback remains largely procedural and detached from interpretation. Design/Approach/Methods This article proposes the Parallel Distributed Processing (PDP)–Innovation, Creativity, and Entrepreneurship Education (ICEE) Learning System as a bridge from educational philosophy to design practice and computational modeling—a distributed architecture that enables education to learn about its own learning. Integrating the Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) principle with the philosophy of ICEE, the model redefines education as a reflexive and self-evolving system capable of transforming technical feedback into epistemic understanding. title: Design and Implementation of Personalized Teacher Professional Development: A Case of an NGO-Based School System in Pakistan
text_snippet: Design and Implementation of Personalized Teacher Professional Development: A Case of an NGO-Based School System in Pakistan Purpose Quality education remains a priority in Pakistan, with teacher competence central to addressing learning gaps. While pre-service teacher training is systematic, in-service professional development is often less standardized and short-term. Alongside the public and private sectors, NGO-based schools are an emerging system that has introduced research-informed practices, yet teacher training still lacks rigor and specificity. This paper explores the development and implementation of personalized teacher professional development using emerging technologies within an NGO-based school system in Pakistan. Design/Approach/Method The model incorporated audio-visual learning modules and school-based audio-visual (AV) studios to support teacher learning. Using a qualitative case study, data were collected through semi-structured interviews with program developers and implementers and were analyzed thematically to understand the design, delivery, and perceived effectiveness of the approach. title: Educators Take Charge: The Potential of Micro-Credentials
text_snippet: Educators Take Charge: The Potential of Micro-Credentials Purpose In this paper, I examine how micro-credentials (MCs) might help address persistent challenges in teacher professional development. I argue that the impact of MC on teacher practice depends both on individual engagement and system-level strategies, policies, and cultural contexts. Design/Approach/Methods The discussion is framed around cases of three teachers. These are intended to illustrate contrasting approaches to and outcomes of professional learning opportunities. These cases are then connected to a broader analysis of implementation strategies that draws on existing research, policy documents, and reform frameworks. Findings MCs have the potential to enhance teacher agency, personalized learning, and relevance when supported by systems and structures designed to value professional judgment and provide time for collaboration. Without systemic change, supportive policies, and cultural change, MCs risk being reduced to yet another compliance activity. Implementation will also vary across centralized and decentralized systems. title: Using Emerging Technologies to Improve English Skills for Women Teachers and Teachers With Disabilities in Rural Rwanda
text_snippet: Using Emerging Technologies to Improve English Skills for Women Teachers and Teachers With Disabilities in Rural Rwanda Purpose The research focuses on how women teachers and teachers with disabilities in Rwanda access and experience the online component of a large-scale donor-funded English language improvement program. Design/Approach/Method The research takes a qualitative case study approach, with 61 participants interviewed in 10 schools in three rural and border districts in Rwanda, in addition to 16 system-level actors. The research team is diverse, with the majority based in Rwanda, and includes experts on gender and disability. Findings Findings indicate that while participants gain confidence and improve their spoken English in the classroom, the complexities of their lives and needs are not easily addressed through donor-funded, large-scale TPD. Well-intentioned adaptations result in unintended consequences that further marginalize teachers or that require localizations and cost-sharing. title: Dual Reconfiguration of Education: How AI Reopens the “End of History” Through the Technology–Governance Dual Curve
text_snippet: Dual Reconfiguration of Education: How AI Reopens the “End of History” Through the Technology–Governance Dual Curve Purpose This article reexamines Fukuyama's “End of History” thesis, arguing that artificial intelligence (AI) has reopened ideological competition and created an unprecedented “legitimacy gap” between exponentially advancing technology and linearly evolving governance. Bridging this gap has become pivotal to addressing many of the global crises we confront today. Design/Approach/Methods The study employs a problem–analysis–solution structure: identifying the legitimacy gap via a “Technology – Governance Dual Curve” model, analyzing three singular transformations and three structural gaps, and proposing solutions through the dual return of humanities/social sciences and education as new-quality infrastructure for human–machine symbiotic societies.
